answer: An aspiring-page record carries `name` (the unresolved page name), `page` (the source page containing the link), `pos` (start of the unresolved link), and `ref` (reference identifying that occurrence). No, the X-Ray lens won't underline it, because `aspiring-page` is a `range`-less object type and those aren't shown.

Page attributes edited through a form and stored as YAML at the top of the page.

--- X-Ray.md ---
Activation | Limitations
* `range`-less objects (`page`, `tag`, `aspiring-page`, `anchor`) aren’t shown — except a tag that occurs only inside a comment, which the indexer gives a range, so X-Ray underlines it (and its card won’t show `inComment`, since `xrayInfo` calls the indexers directly, skipping the comment-marking pass).
* Constructs that the editor renders as a widget may not always show the underline. Hover still works, the tooltip will appear.

--- Tag/aspiring-page.md ---
aspiring-page | Attributes
* `name`: unresolved page name.
* `page`: source page containing the link.
* `pos`: start of the unresolved link.
* `ref`: reference identifying that occurrence.

Records are rebuilt when the source page is indexed. Creating the target page removes its aspiring-page entries.

Tag it | Under the hood
These page attributes are called [[Frontmatter|frontmatter]]. To inspect their source, choose **Edit source** from the form’s ⋯ menu (or **Alt-click** on the form). The form stores a block like this at the very beginning of `Photo Walk`:

```markdown
---
tags: outing
status: planned
date: "2026-06-14"
---
```

The two `---` lines mark the block’s boundaries. Inside, [[YAML]] writes each attribute as `name: value`. Your original notes follow the closing `---`. Move the cursor out of the block to return to the form. You can use either editor. They change the same attributes.
